title: Metadata provider result message
description: The terminal result message that a metadata@1 provider worker sends for one invocation. The host refuses a message with an unknown key, an incorrect status, a missing data object or an incorrect retention record.
$comment: Host-only rules that this schema cannot express: (1) The host counts the lengths of id (128), error (512), identity strings and ids in UTF-16 code units; JSON Schema counts code points. (2) id must be the ID of a current invocation of the same worker; a result for another ID is ignored. (3) The normalized identity (identity, records[].identity, candidates[].identity) has a maximum compact JSON size of 8192 bytes; each candidate has a maximum compact JSON size of 8192 bytes. (4) Identity cross-field rules: kind and type must name the same kind; episodeNumbering or an object episode is permitted only for episode and podcastEpisode; episodeNumbering and episode must be equal when both are present; numbering values must agree with season, episodes, absoluteEpisode and airDate; externalIds must not conflict with ids; after the merge, ids has a maximum of 32 entries. (5) identify candidates need an identity with a known kind and a title; searchAssets candidates need a nonempty id. The operation is not part of the message. (6) A no_match identity must equal the request identity after host normalization. (7) Attribution: name must have a non-space character; url must be a valid absolute https URL with a host and no user information (the pattern is an approximation). A failed attribution is ignored, not refused. (8) The host clamps reuseSeconds per status (match and partial 86400, no_match 3600, ambiguous 600, others 0) and ignores keep and offlineSeconds for statuses other than match and partial. (9) A positive completion receipt needs a nonempty bounded data object and complete host observations. (10) The host coerces some scalar types (for example a numeric ids value or title) to text; this schema states the documented types.

id.description: The invocation ID that the host sent with the request.

error.description: Plain text that explains a failure. The host shows at most 512 characters.

allOf.description: A no_match result reports a complete lookup with no answer. Its data can contain only identity, empty records and candidates arrays, an empty fields object and a retention record. It has no error. Other data or an error prevents a completion receipt.

status.description: The result status. match: fields for the requested entity. partial: some fields; the host asks the next provider for the missing fields. no_match: a complete lookup with no answer. ambiguous: alternatives that need a choice. auth_required, rate_limited, offline, unsupported and error are failures.

data.description: The result data. The host reads only the documented keys.

identity.description: The identity of the entity that the result is for. Without records, the host uses data itself as one record.

records.description: Records, each with its own identity and field claims. The host reads at most 64 records. More than one accepted record for a target makes the result ambiguous.

candidates.description: Identity candidates (identify) or asset candidates (searchAssets). The host reads at most 500 candidates.

cursor.description: An opaque page cursor for a later searchAssets request. Any JSON value.

retryAfterSeconds.description: For rate_limited: the number of seconds before the host can ask this provider again. Without the key, the host waits 60 seconds.

retention.description: What the provider permits the host to keep. Every key is optional. A record with an unknown key or an incorrect value permits nothing: no reuse, no saving and no offline use.

reuseSeconds.description: How long the host can reuse the answer for the same request, account and settings. 0: do not reuse.

keep.description: library: the host can save accepted fields in the media library. memory: the host keeps fields in memory only.

offlineSeconds.description: After the reuse time ends, how long the host can show the answer, labeled as not current, while the provider is offline.

fields.description: Field claims by field name, for example title, description, episodeTitle or artwork. A null value or an empty string is not a claim.

attribution.description: The credit for the data. The host ignores an attribution that is not correct.

evidence.description: How the provider found the match. type label: the match uses only names and titles, so the host does not use it to establish an entity.

record.description: One entity and its field claims.

candidate.description: One identity candidate or asset candidate.

id.description: The provider-local candidate ID. searchAssets candidates need it.

kindName.description: A media kind: movie, episode, series, musicTrack, album, artist, podcast, podcastEpisode, audiobook or unknown. The host compares names without case. Empty means unknown.

externalId.description: A scoped external ID. Movie, series, season and episode IDs are distinct scopes in the same namespace.

episodeNumbering.description: One episode numbering scheme. Use exactly the keys of one scheme.

identity.description: A media identity in the fixed host vocabulary. The host removes other keys. Unknown values stay unknown: use -1 for an unknown number and an empty string for unknown text.

year.description: Movie release year or series start year. -1: unknown.

episode.description: One episode number, or the same object as episodeNumbering.

ids.description: Host ID keys (for example imdb, seriesImdb, tmdbMovie, tvdbEpisode) and their values.
